name: African American Theme House
summary: The African American Theme House, known as Afro House, was established in 1997 to provide a supportive, community-focused environment for Black students at UC Berkeley.

name: Casa Zimbabwe
summary: Casa Zimbabwe (known to many as CZ) has gone through many incarnations over the years since her construction in 1966 as both the first building designed specifically to be a student co-op, and the first in the nation to be co-ed.

name: Cloyne Court
summary: Cloyne is the BSC’s substance-free and academically themed house, available exclusively to UC Berkeley students.

name: Davis House
summary: Originally built in the late 19th century for the attorney of the storied Hearst Family, this resplendent manor was one of the first homes to grace Panoramic Hill.

name: Euclid Hall
summary: 14 Singles - 5 Doubles - 24 Residents 1777 Euclid Ave Berkeley, CA 94709 Euclid is one of the smaller houses—clean, mellow, and cozy. We’re unique in that we have the highest single-to-double ratio in the co-ops: out of nineteen rooms, only five are doubles.

name: Fenwick Weavers Village
summary: Only UC Berkeley students are eligible to live in Fenwick during the Fall and Spring. Fenwick Weavers’ Village is an apartment complex with 1, 2, 3 and 4-Bedroom apartments.

name: Hillegass Parker House
summary: Limited to graduate students and re-entry (age 25 or older) students only. Students must verify their eligibility before they can be assigned.

name: Hoyt Hall
summary: Hello Prospective Hottie! Looking for a place where you can find a community full of the most ambitious and amazing individuals (aka hotties) that you will EVER meet? Well, Hoyt Hall is your best bet!

name: Kidd Hall
summary: 3 singles - 7 Doubles - 17 Residents 2562 Le Conte Avenue Berkeley, CA 94709 Childish and totally awesome at heart, Kidd is a happy-go-lucky house just two blocks from North Gate.

name: Kingman Hall
summary: Kingman Hall, aka Toad Hall, when the weather is just so, is something of a resplendent Victorian manor lodged in the red wooded hills of North Berkeley. Ivy and Morning Glories creep along the sides of the house.

name: Lothlorien
summary: All meals cooked for the house are vegetarian. Personal meat is allowed but meat cannot be purchased with house funds.

name: Northside Apartments
summary: Northside Co-op is located in two adjacent buildings on Le Conte near Kidd, Euclid, Stebbins, and Hoyt co-ops. It is what might be called the final resting place of all good co-opers (hardwood floors, lots of light through multi-paned, old-fashioned windows).

name: Oscar Wilde House
summary: Wilde is America’s first student co-op for lesbian, gay, bisexual, trans, questioning, intersex, asexual, and queer students, and we welcome people of all orientations, gender identities, and expressions.

name: Person of Color Theme House (Castro)
summary: Person of Color Theme House aims to provide housing to low-income, first generation, immigrant and marginalized students of color, as well as people of color who would like to live in more affordable housing.

name: Ridge House
summary: Rising amidst the gothic chapels and tranquility of North Side is the handsome white and green trimmed Tudor–Ridge House.

name: Rochdale Apartments
summary: Only UC Berkeley students are eligible to live in Rochdale during the Fall and Spring. The great thing about the BSC’s largest co-op, Rochdale Village, is that it has the best of both worlds.

name: Sherman Hall
summary: 8 Singles - 13 Doubles - 2 Triples - 40 Residents 2250 Prospect Street Berkeley, CA 94704 Two wheelchair accessible rooms, one has its own bathroom Sherman is women identifying only during the Fall and Spring. Men and women in the summer.

name: Stebbins
summary: 18 Singles - 23 Doubles - 64 Residents 2527 Ridge Road Berkeley, CA 94709 Stebbins Hall is home to students of all backgrounds: veteran co-op’ers and sophomores fresh out of the dorms, junior transfers and foreign exchange students, engineers and sun worshippers, kombucha brewers

name: The Convent
summary: The Convent is in fact a former convent, but the studious, cloistered nuns have long since been replaced by studious, cloistered graduate and re-entry students.

name: Wolf House
